summary: Demo focused on Redwood Console and API controls for request storage, PII redaction, and policy-driven retention. Showed live toggles for ephemeral vs retained request storage, structured PII scrubbing, KMS-backed encryption, and guidance from Redwood Optimize on batching/quantization to meet latency/cost targets. Roadmap items and a trial tenant were agreed.
transcript:
Meeting header: 2026-12-15 14:00 PST | Duration: ~52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Patel (Redwood AE), Samira Cho (Redwood SE), Luis Ortega (Redwood Product), Evan Brooks (Orchard Head of Security), Maya Li (Orchard Platform Engineer), Carlos Mendes (Orchard PM), Priya Shah (Orchard Legal)

Summary section (auto): quick demo of console toggles and API flags, followed by Q&A and next steps. Some background notes: Orchard is evaluating platform for PHI-sensitive triage workflows, looking for ephemeral storage, SOC2 artifacts, and private deployment options.

00:00 Jordan Patel: all right folks, thanks for joining. we'll keep this to about 45 minutes and leave time for q and a. today Samira will walk through the console toggles and then we'll flip to the API examples and the optimize recommendations.
00:18 Samira Cho: hi everyone, thanks. quick note — i'm going to demo request-storage toggles, live redaction rules, and a short run of our optimize suggestion engine. there might be slight lag as i change policies, bear with me.
00:30 Evan Brooks: great, high level first — orchard's constraint is PHI retention window 0 to 30 days depending on patient consent, and we need crypto separation, kms management, and detailed audit logs. also legal wants to ensure egress isn't logged in a way that reveals sensitive ids.
00:52 Jordan Patel: totally, that's exactly why the toggles exist — you can set per-route and per-model retention policies, or set a global default. you can also choose metadata-only storage for analytics while redacting PII from the request body.
01:10 Samira Cho: i'll share my screen — opening Console -> Policies -> Request Storage.
01:22 Samira Cho: here we have four primary modes: retained, ephemeral, metadata-only, and masked. retained is full request storage (encrypted), ephemeral deletes after the request. metadata-only stores tokens, latency, and route tags but strips request content. masked attempts structured redaction based on rule sets.
01:45 Carlos Mendes: masked — is that regex-based only, or do you use an ML redactor?
01:51 Samira Cho: good question. it's hybrid — rule-first regex patterns for known schemas + tokenizers, plus a lightweight neural redaction pass for ambiguous PHI. we call out high-confidence entities and then you can configure auto-delete vs manual review.
02:08 Maya Li: how deterministic is neural redaction — we can't have inconsistent redaction across requests for the same patient id.
02:15 Samira Cho: we provide deterministic hashing + KMS salt keys so the same PII maps to the same masked token when enabled, but you can also opt for irreversible redaction if you want no mapping retained.
02:34 Priya Shah: and where are those salts stored? on customer KMS?
02:38 Samira Cho: yes, for Private deployments we integrate with your KMS/HSM. for Hosted, we support customer-managed KMS via key import or external HSM connectors — the salt is never stored in plaintext in Redwood logs.
02:55 Evan Brooks: good. show me an example — can you redact an MRN or SSN inline?
03:03 Samira Cho: sure — i'll run a test through the API playground here. calling /v1/generate with header x-redwood-request-storage: masked and redaction-profile: health-ph.
03:20 API call (simulated): payload includes patient name: "Maria Gonzales", MRN: "MRN-128934", complaint: "abdominal pain".
03:30 Transcription glitch: Speaker label flips briefly -> Speaker 2: uh-huh.
03:36 Samira Cho: response returns generated text; request storage entry shows masked MRN -> {{mrn_0}} and name hashed to patient_1 (deterministic). note: original content is stored only if you selected retained and you have KMS key.
03:55 Evan Brooks: so if we choose masked + irreversible, the original MRN is not recoverable?
04:02 Samira Cho: correct, irreversible redaction removes the original and stores only the redacted artifact with no mapping.
04:12 Jordan Patel: also important — you can scope these rules by route or model and even by tag. so triage endpoints can be ephemeral while analytics endpoints are metadata-only.
04:28 Maya Li: latency impact? will redaction slow us down on high qps endpoints?
04:32 Samira Cho: we've optimized the redaction pipeline — regex rules are negligible, the neural pass runs async for >100ms tail in worst case. for strict latency SLOs we recommend metadata-only or pre-token-level scrubbing client-side. also Redwood Optimize will suggest batching or smaller context to keep token cost low.
05:00 Luis Ortega: side note — Optimize can surface cost/latency tradeoffs per route; e.g., suggest quantized model variant + batching for asynchronous workflows to meet 99th percentile latency target.
05:18 Evan Brooks: we need tamper-evident audit logs for compliance — can Redwood supply immutable audit trails?
05:22 Samira Cho: yes, audit logs are append-only, time-stamped, and can be forwarded to your SIEM via syslog or Kafka. we also sign entries and can push to customer-owned S3 with object-lock for retention policies.
05:38 Priya Shah: what about legal discovery — if subpoena demands request content, can we retrieve the original when masked?
05:46 Samira Cho: retrieval depends on your retention setting: if masked+deterministic mapping exists and you have KMS key, you can reverse map. if irreversible redaction was used, there's no way to get the original. we log access and require role check approvals.
06:10 Jordan Patel: let's demo the Console policy rule editor — i'll pass control to Samira.
06:18 Samira Cho: here — rule editor UI, you can create a rule: match path /api/triage/*, match header x-client-consent = yes, action = metadata-only; else match PHI regex -> redaction profile = irreversible. i'll save and apply. applying policy is zero-downtime and policy rollout can be staged.
06:45 Carlos Mendes: can we version rules and roll back?
06:48 Samira Cho: yes, policy versioning with canary rollouts to specific models or capacity pools. you get diffs and a dry-run option.
07:00 Maya Li: what about the SDK — can we override per-request via a header?
07:04 Samira Cho: yes, both SDK and HTTP API support request-level overrides — x-redwood-request-storage, x-redwood-redaction-mode. recommended to gate overrides behind a service account role.
07:20 Evan Brooks: metrics — if we go metadata-only, will we still see token counts and cost metrics per request?
07:24 Samira Cho: yes, cost telemetry and token breakdown are always available; only request content is suppressed. you can also enable sampled content for debug with access controls.
07:42 Jordan Patel: quick tangent — private deployment. Orchard mentioned wanting a VPC private control plane. walk through differences.
07:50 Samira Cho: private gives you customer-managed control plane with optional on-prem package. in private mode logs can be forwarded directly to your ingest pipeline; KMS integration is mandatory for secret handling. some customers run a hybrid: control plane in their VPC, compute in our dedicated cluster with VPC peering.
08:12 Evan Brooks: do you support air-gapped on-prem?
08:15 Samira Cho: yes, we have an on-prem package; it requires additional ops work but supports HSM, internal KMS, and SASL authentication for log shipping.
08:30 Priya Shah: encryption at rest standards?
08:33 Luis Ortega: AES-256-FIPS for storage; keys are rotated per your KMS policy; we publish our cipher suite.
08:40 Maya Li: ok, let's try a redaction edge case — free-text patient notes with embedded PHI in odd formats.
08:48 Samira Cho: sending a longer free-text sample to the test endpoint.
09:05 Samira Cho: system detected phone numbers, dates, and possible patient names. neural redactor flagged low-confidence token 'Gonz' which in manual review we confirmed as last name. you can add custom entity dictionaries in the policy editor so it is consistently caught.
09:30 Evan Brooks: show me how to add that dictionary quickly.
09:35 Samira Cho: settings -> dictionaries -> new -> upload CSV of names -> scope to policy -> save. now I will reprocess sample in dry-run and show diff.
09:56 System note (auto): dry-run flagged 12 matches, suggested irreversible redaction for MRNs, masked for dates.
10:10 Carlos Mendes: what's the storage cost delta between retained and metadata-only?
10:14 Samira Cho: highly workload dependent; metadata-only typically reduces storage by 80-95% because we store tokens and route metadata only. retained is full payload stored compressed; Redwood Optimize will give a per-route cost estimate once we ingest sample traffic.
10:30 Evan Brooks: on compliance, we need SOC2 plus ISO/IEC 27001 artifacts — are those available for Hosted?
10:37 Jordan Patel: we publish SOC2 Type II and ISO artifacts to our security portal for customers after an NDA. i'll include the link in follow-up.
10:50 Priya Shah: redaction logs — who can see the pre-redacted content in the console?
10:55 Samira Cho: access is governed by RBAC. only roles with 'full-audit' can view pre-redaction in dry-run or if retention policy allowed original content; all access is audited.
11:10 Maya Li: let's talk about API-level toggles for ephemeral storage — we want an SDK param to always enforce ephemeral for triage endpoints.
11:18 Samira Cho: sample: client.generate({model: 'rwd-triage-1', request_storage: 'ephemeral', redaction: 'irreversible'}) — that pin on the request header overrides default policy unless the account policy prohibits overrides.
11:38 Evan Brooks: can we force server-side blocking of overrides?
11:41 Samira Cho: yes, admin policies can disable per-request overrides; only account admins can change that, and we log attempts.
11:52 Jordan Patel: walk-through of the Optimize suggestions — Luis?
11:55 Luis Ortega: sure — Optimize ingests telemetry and provides suggestions: e.g., enable dynamic batching on model rwd-triage-1, reduce context window from 2048 to 1024 for short triage prompts, and switch to a 4-bit quantized variant for background classification jobs. it simulates cost/latency impact and offers a one-click rollout.
12:20 Carlos Mendes: will quantization affect hallucination or generation quality for clinical text?
12:26 Luis Ortega: small risk for generative detail; for classification or intent detection it's negligible. we also support evals tied to prompt sets; you can run a regression check after a rollout.
12:40 Evan Brooks: for the trial we want: 1) policy-driven ephemeral for triage, 2) metadata-only for analytics, 3) irreversible redaction for identified PHI. can Redwood provision that?
12:50 Jordan Patel: yes, Samira will provision a trial tenant. we'll enable VPC peering and hook up KMS with your test key.
13:05 Priya Shah: we'll need a DPIA and data flow diagram for legal review. can you produce an architecture doc?
13:11 Jordan Patel: yes — i'll include architecture diagram and a DPIA template.
13:20 Maya Li: small thing — we'd like to sample 1% of raw requests for debug, but only for whitelisted service accounts. is that supported?
13:26 Samira Cho: yes, sampling with allowlist, and we flag sampled items in the audit stream; samples are only available to full-audit role and have a TTL.
13:40 Evan Brooks: any third-party processors involved? we need names for the contract.
13:45 Jordan Patel: we use cloud infra partners for compute; specifics will depend on deployment (region). we'll send a list as part of the security pack.
13:55 Carlos Mendes: timeline — if we like the trial, what's typical onboarding for Dedicated or Private?
13:59 Jordan Patel: Dedicated is usually 4-8 weeks for capacity provisioning; Private/VPC with KMS/HSM tends to be 6-12 weeks depending on customer ops.
14:12 Priya Shah: last question: do you allow field-level retention policies? e.g., keep medication list for 180 days but delete SSN immediately.
14:20 Samira Cho: yes — policy engine can target JSON paths or schema fields with per-field TTLs and actions (mask, irreversible, retain).
14:34 Jordan Patel: okay let's recap action items. Jordan will send security pack; Samira will provision trial tenant; Maya to send sample payloads; Priya to provide legal checklist. we aim to reconvene after trial in two weeks.
14:52 Evan Brooks: thanks everyone — this was helpful.
14:56 Meeting end.

Notes on transcription quality: speaker labels occasionally flip and some punctuation is missing; there are a few ASR mis-hears (e.g., MRN sometimes transcribed as 'M R N' or 'M R N one two').

References/shared artifacts mentioned: security whitepaper (link to be shared), DPIA template (link), trial tenant provisioning ticket in Redwood Console (ticket to be created), sample payload CSV (from Orchard).
